title: Reverse Mortgage Stabilization Act of 2013
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Reverse Mortgage Stabilization Act of 2013 - Amends the National Housing Act, with respect to mortgage insurance for home equity conversion mortgages (reverse mortgages) of elderly homeowners, to authorize the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to establish, by notice or mortgagee letter, any additional or alternative requirements determined necessary to improve the fiscal safety and soundness of the reverse mortgage program.

Declares that such requirements shall take effect upon issuance.

summary.headline: This 2013 law lets the Housing and Urban Development Department add or change rules for federally insured reverse mortgages to strengthen the program's finances.
summary.what_it_does: It amends the National Housing Act, which governs federal mortgage insurance for reverse mortgages, also called home equity conversion mortgages. It lets the HUD Secretary set extra or different requirements through a notice or mortgagee letter when needed to improve the program's fiscal safety and soundness. Those requirements take effect as soon as HUD issues them.

who_it_affects.group: Elderly homeowners with federally insured reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: HUD can change the rules for their loans through notices or mortgagee letters, and those changes take effect when issued.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders and mortgage servicers that offer federally insured reverse mortgages
who_it_affects.how: They must follow any new or alternative HUD requirements issued under this authority as soon as they are published.

who_it_affects.group: Future borrowers considering a reverse mortgage
who_it_affects.how: Loan terms and eligibility rules may change over time as HUD uses this authority.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on August 9, 2013. Each new HUD requirement takes effect when HUD issues it.
